articles.title: TMC Crisis: Election Commission Freezes Party Name and Symbol, Both Factions Submit New Options
articles.description: West Bengal politics has entered a fresh phase of uncertainty after the Election Commission reportedly froze the Trinamool Congress party name and its existing election symbol with immediate effect. The development comes ahead of the upcoming assembly bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, scheduled for October 6. Following the Commission’s direction, both rival factions were asked to submit three options each for a new party name and election symbol. The Ritabrata Banerjee faction has reportedly proposed the names National Trinamool Congress Democratic, Trinamool Congress and West Bengal Trinamool Congress. It has also submitted three symbol options, including a blackboard and a torch. The names and symbols proposed by the Mamata Banerjee faction have not yet been made public, according to the information in the report. The existing TMC name and the familiar twin-flowers-on-grass symbol cannot be used by either faction until further orders. The dispute has therefore moved into a crucial phase, with both sides awaiting the Election Commission’s decision on their proposed alternatives. The Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls have added significance because both seats became vacant after their respective elected representatives vacated them. The results are scheduled for October 9. The Election Commission’s decision has also triggered a political response from Congress leader Rahul Gandhi. In a social media post, Gandhi questioned the decision and alleged a repeated pattern involving political parties and election symbols. These are political allegations and represent his stated position, rather than an established finding.

articles.title: US Yields, Crude Oil prices cool | Tata Group Stocks In Focus on Tata Sons Tata Trusts Split
articles.description: Wall Street rallied on Thursday, with the Dow gaining 0.6%, the S&P 500 rising 1.1% and the Nasdaq surging 1.7%, as lower US Treasury yields and easing oil prices supported risk appetite. The US 10-year yield pulled back to 4.73%, while the 30-year and 2-year yields also declined. Brent crude eased to around $105 a barrel, with Saudi Arabia reportedly sending crude through ship-to-ship transfers. In India, the Nifty rose for the second straight day, while the Sensex ended slightly lower. Midcaps rebounded strongly, with the Midcap index gaining 1%. FIIs remained net sellers, offloading ₹3,208.76 crore in equities, while DIIs were net buyers with purchases worth ₹3,617.75 crore. Tata Group stocks are likely to remain in focus after Tata Sons reappointed N Chandrasekaran as Chairman. The move has also triggered public disagreement from Tata Trusts over his reappointment and the proposed listing of Tata Sons.
